Today, I’m excited to announce that OLIPOP has hired a new CEO! I took the CEO title when OLIPOP PBC was founded to ensure that I could use the seat to guide our adherence to the mission and founding vision. Young brands can easily lose their way as they raise capital and weather the million different death jumps required when starting from zero. Operating competitively while maintaining our integrity has always required more time, effort, and innovation. We’ve invested deeply in our people and culture, funded clinical research into microbiome, digestive, and metabolic health, and held a high bar for formulation and efficacy. We’ve prioritized long-term, sustainable growth over short-term numbers or a quick exit. We could have taken shortcuts to grow faster—but when your mission is to make human life better, they simply aren’t worth it. I’m deeply grateful for and proud of what we’ve accomplished. The OLIPOP team is among the finest I’ve ever worked with, and the letters we receive from families and customers are profound. I still formulate every new flavor from scratch. With OLIPOP now in nearly one in four households, we’re genuinely moving the needle on people’s wellbeing. Throughout this journey I’ve worn a large number of hats. Founder, CEO, Formulator, and Chair of the Board. It’s been a dynamic balance and several full-time jobs all in one. Honestly, not bad for what used to be a scrappy kid who wore sweatpants to investor pitches and would sometimes forget to talk about the business because he was rambling about the microbiome and brain/gut axis. As OLIPOP has surpassed the half-billion mark and professionalized, I’ve been reflecting on where I can have the greatest impact going forward. I want to focus my energy where I have the most passion and can contribute most meaningfully, while bringing in a counterweight to strengthen the areas I’m stepping away from—adding horsepower rather than simply reallocating focus. Given all that, I decided it was time to explore bringing in a new CEO—someone who could be a powerhouse operator and help drive the business in a mission-aligned way, while allowing me to double down on innovation, research, culture, marketing, thought leadership, and strategy. That search led to Christian Patiño Webb, who will be joining us this month as CEO. Not only has Christian led gobsmacking profitable growth as the outgoing CEO at Electrolit, but he’s also a highly principled and humble culture-first leader. Getting to know Christian over the last six months, I was deeply impressed that someone with such a strong track record of performance could also have the self-discipline to put team and values above all else. I’m excited to partner with Christian to unlock our next chapter of growth and impact, and I’m glad to take solace in finding a leader that I know won’t push to compromise mission or quality as we endeavor our way to reach the next summit.

results.title: OLIPOP CEO Ben Goodwin at WSJ Global Food Forum | OLIPOP PBC posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.author: OLIPOP PBC
highlights:
OLIPOP CEO Ben Goodwin at WSJ Global Food Forum | OLIPOP PBC posted on the topic | LinkedIn
...
What happens when you challenge the idea that soda has to stay the same? For years, our Co-Founder, CEO, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin, has been exploring a simple but ambitious belief: that one of the world’s most beloved beverages could evolve into something more functional, more intentional, and better aligned with how people want to feel today. That vision helped spark OLIPOP, and it’s why we were honored to see Ben take the stage at The Wall Street Journal Global Food Forum alongside an incredible group of leaders shaping the future of food, health, and agriculture. In his session, “The Market for Prebiotic Soda Is Bubbling, OLIPOP Is on Top,” 🫧 Ben shared insights from OLIPOP’s journey—from early formulation and category creation to scaling a brand that’s helping redefine what modern soda can be. The conversation also explored the opportunities and challenges that come with balancing innovation, growth, and impact. A special thank you to Ben Cohen for leading such a thoughtful and engaging discussion, and to The Wall Street Journal team for creating a forum that brings together important conversations about the future of our food system. We're grateful to be part of this dialogue and excited for what’s ahead. ➡️ Tune in to Ben's session here - https://lnkd.in/g7Z429TH
